svg.title: The Title Cost Ladder From Guesswork to Courthouse Search
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-title-cost-ladder; chapter number: 6; title: The Title Cost Ladder From Guesswork to Courthouse Search; subtitle: What a mistake, a probate and a records search each cost; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Guessed title call; value: 500000; display: $400,000-$500,000; conversion: Avoided by working every interest in fractions and never guessing; detail: The Landman Class instructor cites mistakes of this size and says one guess can lose the client and the whole firm's jobs.; label: Simple probate as curative; value: 4000; display: $3,000-$4,000; conversion: Can exceed the value of a 0.1 net-acre interest; detail: Matt Sands and Justin Williams note this is why affidavits of heirship get used. Ask the operator which document it will accept before drafting.; label: File Viewer document package; value: 100; display: 300 views for $100; conversion: Pull only the instruments the chain actually needs; detail: Digital courthouse tool cited alongside Courthouse Direct for title runs.; label: Courthouse Direct legal-description search; value: 63.9; display: $63.90 for 439 results; conversion: Treat a zero-result search as an input error first; detail: Paul Cones ran a live Reeves County search and read out the charge after first typing an entry into the wrong box.; label: Courthouse Direct base fee; value: 20; display: $20 plus $0.10 per record; conversion: Entry cost before per-record charges; detail: Clean title runs take 1-2 weeks, complex chains 3-5 weeks.; caption: A search costs tens of dollars, curative costs thousands, and a guessed fraction costs hundreds of thousands.; assumptions note: Stages are ordered by cost, not by workflow volume. Where a range was quoted, the value uses the high end of that range.; note: Attributed to Landman Class (ibeQr-rDmZ4), Matt Sands with Justin Williams (sB8BNPnN_Os, zoP-dgL5D7M) and CourthouseAcademy with Paul Cones (822U1_i8V5Q) on YouTube.

text.title: The Title Cost Ladder From Guesswork to Courthouse Search
text.tspan: The Title Cost Ladder From Guesswork to Courthouse

rect.title: label: Guessed title call; value: 500000; display: $400,000-$500,000; conversion: Avoided by working every interest in fractions and never guessing; detail: The Landman Class instructor cites mistakes of this size and says one guess can lose the client and the whole firm's jobs.

label: Simple probate as curative; value: 4000; display: $3,000-$4,000; conversion: Can exceed the value of a 0.1 net-acre interest; detail: Matt Sands and Justin Williams note this is why affidavits of heirship get used. Ask the operator which document it will accept before drafting.

label: File Viewer document package; value: 100; display: 300 views for $100; conversion: Pull only the instruments the chain actually needs; detail: Digital courthouse tool cited alongside Courthouse Direct for title runs.

label: Courthouse Direct legal-description search; value: 63.9; display: $63.90 for 439 results; conversion: Treat a zero-result search as an input error first; detail: Paul Cones ran a live Reeves County search and read out the charge after first typing an entry into the wrong box.
label: Courthouse Direct base fee; value: 20; display: $20 plus $0.10 per record; conversion: Entry cost before per-record charges; detail: Clean title runs take 1-2 weeks, complex chains 3-5 weeks.

text.title: Assumptions: Stages are ordered by cost, not by workflow volume. Where a range was quoted, the value uses the high end of that range.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Stages are ordered by cost, not by workflow volume. Where a range was quoted, the value uses the high end of that range.
